beyond_integration.config.comment.workst:
Enabled workstations: remove an id to disable that workstation
Valid ids: craft, anvil, cut, grind, smith, enchant
Example: enabled=["craft","anvil"] -> only craft and anvil can be opened

Workstation sacrifice activation (optional balance, disabled by default)
When enabled, workstations other than crafting (craft) must be activated by sacrificing the matching vanilla workstation (network-wide, one activation unlocks the whole network)
Enable sacrifice activation: when true, clicking an unactivated workstation in the BD terminal will attempt to sacrifice (consume network items) instead of opening it

Sacrifice cost per workstation (format: workstationId:itemId:count)
Items are consumed from network storage; workstations not listed require no sacrifice
Example: anvil:minecraft:anvil:1 -> anvil workstation requires sacrificing 1 anvil

Ticks between full ammo rescans and pushes to clients

Ticks between SW ammo/FE diff checks and pushes to clients
beyond_integration.config.comment.energy: Equipment-slot item network charging settings (chargeable armor + main/offhand tools & weapons)
beyond_integration.config.energy_ammo.ch: Equipment-slot item auto-charging (chargeable armor / curios + main/offhand tools & weapons)
beyond_integration.config.comment.energy:
Enable auto-charging equipment-slot items: worn chargeable armor, accessories (Curios) and main/offhand tools & weapons are topped up from the player's primary network FE storage (maid: bound network)
Example: charge_enabled=true -> charge periodically while holding or wearing chargeable items
Ticks between each network charge attempt
FE extracted from network per charge attempt (fixed amount for RATE / flat part for PERCENTAGE_PLUS_RATE; capped by item's missing energy)
Charge mode: RATE = fixed charge_rate per interval; PERCENTAGE = charge_percentage% of max energy capacity; PERCENTAGE_PLUS_RATE = percentage + fixed rate
Percentage of max energy capacity used by percentage modes (0-100)

Auto-charge whitelist: supports item IDs (e.g. minecraft:diamond_sword) and tags (prefixed with #, e.g. #forge:tools); matched items are chargeable even if not tools/weapons; defaults include wireless terminals from AE2 / AE2WTLib / RS / WCWT
Enable Curios accessory auto-charging: chargeable curios worn by players and maids are topped up every interval (requires Curios)
Enable maid-exclusive accessory auto-charging: chargeable baubles in Touhou Little Maid's slots are topped up every interval (requires Touhou Little Maid)
Anvil XP charge mode: LEVEL = vanilla levels (network XP tops up player levels first), POINTS = fixed XP points (network XP pays first)
LEVEL mode 'too expensive' level cap (40 = vanilla default, 2147483647 = no cap)
POINTS mode 'too expensive' XP point cap (9223372036854775807 = no cap)

Enchantment max level mode (OFF = vanilla clamp, PLUS = over-level merging 5+5=6 without cap, ADDITIVE = same enchantment levels add up 5+5=10)
Example: anvil.breakMaxLevelMode=ADDITIVE -> two Sharpness V books make Sharpness X

Ignore enchantment conflicts: conflicting enchantments are kept and can coexist (each conflicting enchantment adds the conflictPenalty cost)
Example: ignoreConflict=true -> Sharpness V and Smite V can coexist on one item

Ignore enchantment applicability: enchantments that normally cannot be applied are allowed, like creative mode (each violation adds the supportPenalty cost)
Example: ignoreSupport=true -> a hoe can receive Sharpness V

Fully unrestricted: enables breakMaxLevelMode=PLUS, ignoreConflict and ignoreSupport at once (percentage bonuses stack, see the Percent options)
Example: unrestricted=true -> all limits removed, cost multiplied by (100 + sum of enabled percents)/100

Fixed cost per conflicting enchantment (base value, applied before percentage multipliers)
Example: conflictPenalty=2 -> 2 conflicting enchantments add +4

Fixed cost per inapplicable (violating) enchantment (base value)
Example: supportPenalty=5 -> 1 violating enchantment adds +5

Percentage cost bonus for ignoring conflicts (multiplier = (100 + sum of enabled percents)/100, 100 = extra x1)
Example: conflictPercent=50 with ignoreConflict -> enchantment cost x1.5

Percentage cost bonus for ignoring applicability (multiplier as above, percents add up)
Example: supportPercent=50 with ignoreSupport -> enchantment cost x1.5

Percentage cost bonus for breaking the level cap (PLUS/ADDITIVE) (multiplier as above, percents add up)
Example: breakLevelPercent=30 -> enchantment cost x1.3

Percentage cost bonus for fully unrestricted mode (multiplier = (100 + sum of enabled percents)/100)
Example: unrestrictedPercent=100 with unrestricted -> cost x2
beyond_integration.config.comment.enchan: Enchantment table workstation settings
Enchant power source: FIXED = fixed power (fixedPower), NETWORK_XP = power from network XP fluid (xpPerPower points each), PLAYER_LEVEL = power from player levels (levelPerPower levels each)
FIXED mode power (vanilla cap 15; up to 100 with uncapPower)
NETWORK_XP mode: XP points per 1 power
PLAYER_LEVEL mode: player levels per 1 power

Allow enchanting already-enchanted items: add new compatible enchantments or upgrade existing ones (low to high)
Conflicts are controlled by ignoreConflict
Allow adding enchantments that conflict with existing ones (works with ignoreEnchanted for enchanted items)
Free enchanting: no fuel consumed (the fuel slot may still be filled)
Remove the level requirement: no longer requires player levels to reach the cost, charged by XP points instead (network XP first)
Remove the power cap 15 -> 100 (cost formula switches to the unclamped version)
Cost percentage: actual deduction is scaled by this percent (100 = full price, 50 = half price)
Allow treasure enchantments from the enchanting table (e.g. Mending, Frost Walker; vanilla loot-only)
Server-side switch: hover preview (sends the list of enchantments to gain)
Server-side switch: refresh button (rerolls the three slot candidates)
Fuel consumed by the refresh button (0 = free; noLapis/creative are also free)
beyond_integration.config.comment.bd_twe: BD modifications (tweaks applied to Beyond Dimensions)
Enable XP Rod (beyonddimensions:xp_exchange_item) tweaks: target level cap / batched granting / direct granting (disable = vanilla BD behavior)

Burn the Net Terminal as a furnace input to smelt ALL smeltable items in its bound network
When enabled: put a Beyond Dimensions Net Terminal in the furnace input slot (fuel the furnace); it is cooked into itself (NBT kept, NOT consumed) - taking the terminal out of the furnace then triggers smelting ALL smeltable items in its bound network at once; recipe XP is stored as network XP fluid (1 XP = 20 mB)
Default: disabled

Max target level settable on the XP Rod (keep-mode target level)
Default 238609312 = highest level reachable through legal XP gains
Example: max_target_level=100000 -> allow keep target up to level 100000

Max XP granted per tick (batched granting to avoid int-overflow/precision issues)
Default Integer.MAX_VALUE-1 = effectively one shot per tick
Set a smaller value for smooth batched granting, 0 = also no batching
Example: grant_batch_size=1000000 -> grant at most 1,000,000 XP per tick until the target is reached

XP granting path:
BATCH = batched giveExperiencePoints (max level 238609312)
DIRECT = direct level set + progress + XP difference settlement (not bound by vanilla level formulas)
Example: grant_mode=DIRECT -> level/progress are set directly, difference paid from network
beyond_integration.config.comment.auto_t: Auto totem settings (uses totems from your network only)
Automatically use a totem from your network when dying
Cooldown between auto-totem uses (seconds, 0 = no cooldown)
Damage types that will NOT trigger auto-totem (msgId or minecraft:msgId)

Whether auto-totem respects the vanilla BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY rule (damage like void/out_of_world and /kill never triggers totem)
true = keep vanilla behavior; false = allow triggering on such damage (damage_blacklist still applies)

Restore the player's reduced maximum health when auto-totem triggers (removes all negative max_health attribute modifiers, e.g. from mods/effects)
true = restore the reduced max-health cap

Heal the player to full health when auto-totem triggers
false = keep vanilla totem behavior (1 HP + regeneration buff)
beyond_integration.config.comment.revive: SetHealth revive settings (uses totems from your network only)
Event-based revive: revives on the death event (when false the handler is not registered, zero event cost)
Mixin-based revive: injects the vanilla totem check and revives before the death flow reaches die() (when false it does not intervene)
Cooldown between revive uses (seconds, 0 = no cooldown; shared by both implementations)
Damage types that will NOT trigger revive (msgId or minecraft:msgId)

Whether revive respects the vanilla BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY rule (damage like void/out_of_world and /kill never triggers revive)
true = keep vanilla behavior; false = allow triggering on such damage (damage_blacklist still applies)

Consume extra totems when the death cannot be explained by the vanilla damage chain (direct setHealth kill)
true = extra cost (conservative: unconfirmed deaths are treated as setHealth)
Extra totems consumed on setHealth deaths (total cost = 1 + this value)

Restore the player's reduced maximum health when revive triggers (removes all negative max_health attribute modifiers)
true = restore the reduced max-health cap

Heal the player to full health when revive triggers
false = keep vanilla totem behavior (1 HP + regeneration buff)

Reset the entity death time on revive (deathTime/hurtTime/pose) to cancel death presentation and removal timing
true = reset death time
